diagnostic_evidence.quote: Denote by $\Ss_n^X$  the family of all linear sampling algorithms $S_k^X$ in $L_2(U,X;\mu)$ of the form \eqref{S_k} with $k \le n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The inequality \varrho_n \ll error(S_{c_3 n}) is false because \varrho_n is an infimum over algorithms using at most n sample points, whereas S_{c_3 n} uses c_3 n points (c_3 \ge 3284). An algorithm with more points can have smaller error, so its error does not upper-bound \varrho_n.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reindex the algorithm, e.g. use S_{c_3 n'} with n'=\lfloor n/c_3\rfloor to obtain an algorithm with at most n points, or remove the invalid intermediate inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed chain in Theorem thm:varrho_n(iii) and Theorem theorem:varrho_n><(iii) is invalid, though the final rate can be recovered by reindexing.
issues.title: Sampling n-width bounded by an algorithm using c_3 n points
issues.why_classification: A short reindexing repairs the statement and preserves the final convergence rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The set B^q(M,N) is defined by ||v||_{H_{X,\sigma}}\le M and \sigma satisfying ||\sigma^{-1}||_{\ell_q}\le N. It does not scale with N; scaling v by M gives B^q(M,N)=M B^q(1,N), not MN B^q(1,1). The factor N must come from bounding the tail sum of d_s^2 using the \ell_q bound on \sigma^{-1}, which the proof omits.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false equality by the scaling ||v||\le M and use ||\sigma^{-1}||_{\ell_q}\le N to estimate the tail sum, e.g. \sum_{s\ge m} \sigma_s^{-2} \ll N^2 m^{1-2/q}, yielding the stated rates.
issues.overall_effect: The proof does not establish the claimed convergence rates in Theorem thm:varrho_n and its applications.
issues.title: False scaling of B^q(M,N) by MN in proof of Theorem thm:varrho_n
issues.why_classification: The final rates survive and the repair is a contained tail-sum estimate, but it is a nontrivial missing argument central to the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: With the chosen \sigma_s = s^{1/q}(\log(s+1))^\varepsilon, the Kolmogorov width is d_n \asymp M \sigma_{n+1}^{-1} = M n^{-1/q}(\log n)^{-\varepsilon}, independent of N. To obtain the claimed MN factor, \sigma must be scaled by a factor proportional to N^{-1} so that ||\sigma^{-1}||_{\ell_q}\le N while d_n gains the factor N.

failure_location.quote:
To prove the lower bound, one can take $\bsigma=(\sigma_s)_{s \in \NN}$ with 
 $\sigma_s = s^{1/q} (\log (s+1))^{\varepsilon}$, and prove that $\bsigma^{-1} \in \ell_q(\NN)$ and  that by Theorem \ref{thm:rho_n=},
 \begin{align*}
  \varrho_n(B_{X,\bsigma}^q(M,N), L_2(U,X;\mu))
  \ &= \  
   \varrho_n(B_{\CC,\bsigma}^q(M,N), L_2(U,\CC;\mu)) 
   \\&
 \ \ge \
 d_n(B_{\CC,\bsigma}^q(M,N), L_2(U,\CC;\mu)) 
 \asymp 
 MN n^{-1/q} (\log n)^{-\varepsilon}.
 \end{align*}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Scale the constructed sequence, e.g. take \sigma_s = N^{-1} s^{1/q}(\log(s+1))^\varepsilon (or a constant multiple) so that ||\sigma^{-1}||_{\ell_q}\le N and d_n \asymp MN n^{-1/q}(\log n)^{-\varepsilon}.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound in the quasi-optimality relation (lowerbound) is not established as written.
issues.title: Missing N scaling in lower-bound construction for quasi-optimality
issues.why_classification: A single scaling correction fixes the construction and preserves the quasi-optimality claim.

issues.failure_explanation: The defined \rho need not be (b,\xi)-admissible. Indeed, \sum_j b_j \rho_j = (\xi/(4\sqrt{\eta!})) ||b||_{\ell_p}^{p+1}, which can exceed \xi when ||b||_{\ell_p}^{p+1} > 4\sqrt{\eta!}. The assumptions only require \rho_j>1 and do not imply this inequality. Since the holomorphic property only gives bounds for admissible \rho, the subsequent weighted \ell_2-summability conclusion for the \sigma built from this \rho is unsupported.

failure_location.quote:
Let $\eta\in\NN$ and let the sequence $\brho=(\rho_j)_{j \in \NN}$ be defined by
	$$
	\rho_j:=b_j^{p-1}\frac{\xi}{4\sqrt{\eta!}} \norm{\bb}{\ell_p(\NN)}.
	$$
	Assume that $\bb$ is a decreasing sequence and that $b_j^{p-1}\frac{\xi}{4\sqrt{\eta!}} \norm{\bb}{\ell_p(\NN)}>1$ for all $j\in \NN$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the definition of \rho (e.g. replace ||b||_{\ell_p} by ||b||_{\ell_p}^{-p}) or add the missing condition ||b||_{\ell_p}^{p+1} \le 4\sqrt{\eta!} to ensure admissibility.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma weighted summability holomorphic and the downstream Theorem sampling-lognormal-holomorphic are not established as stated.
issues.title: Holomorphic lemma uses a non-admissible sequence \rho
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local formula/condition correction, but it is necessary for the proof and affects a key lemma and its application.
